title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: From midnight runs to symbolic candle lightings, Chapman University's traditions blend its religious heritage with modern student life in the heart of Orange.

cards.title: The Midnight Undie Run
cards.subtitle: A finals week stress-reliever through Old Towne Orange
cards.notes: At midnight on the Wednesday of finals week, students gather at Schmid Gate in their underwear to run to the Orange Circle and back.
cards.short_summary: A semi-annual midnight run through the streets of Orange to relieve finals week stress.
cards.evidence_claim: The Undie Run is a student tradition held at midnight on the Wednesday of finals week, where students run from Schmid Gate to the Orange Circle.
cards.source_title: Why We Undie Run: Experts say the Chapman tradition is a display of communal rebellion
cards.access_notes: Occurs at midnight during finals week; public streets are often closed by police for safety.

cards.title: Alumni Candle Lighting Ceremony
cards.subtitle: Passing the 'Flame of Knowledge' to new Panthers
cards.notes: During orientation, alumni light candles for incoming students around the Four Pillars fountain to symbolize the passing of knowledge.
cards.short_summary: A symbolic ceremony where alumni welcome new students by passing a literal flame in the campus center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Alumni Candle Lighting Ceremony is a tradition held on the last night of orientation in the Attallah Piazza.
cards.source_title: Alumni Welcome Family Members into the Panther Fold With Candle Lighting Ceremony
cards.access_notes: Held annually during New Student Orientation in late August.

cards.title: Orientation Fountain Hopping
cards.subtitle: A late-night splash for incoming freshmen
cards.notes: Incoming students often jump into campus fountains on the night before classes start to ensure academic success for the next four years.
cards.short_summary: An unofficial rite of passage where freshmen splash through campus fountains before their first day of class.
cards.evidence_claim: Fountain hopping is a ritual where freshmen splash into campus fountains the night before classes to ensure success.
cards.source_title: Fall 2024 Vol. II by Chapbook Magazine
cards.access_notes: Typically occurs late at night during orientation week.

cards.title: The Cheverton Silver Bowl
cards.subtitle: The university's highest undergraduate honor
cards.notes: The names of top graduates are engraved on a silver bowl and bronze cup, gifts from the Class of 1929, on display in Argyros Forum.
cards.short_summary: A permanent exhibit of the university's most prestigious student award, featuring trophies from 1929.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cheverton Award trophies, a bronze cup and silver bowl, are on permanent exhibit in the Argyros Forum.
cards.source_title: SGA President Rachel Berns '24 Named Cheverton Award Winner
cards.access_notes: The trophies are visible to the public inside the Argyros Forum student union.

cards.title: Touching the Panther for Luck
cards.subtitle: A game-day ritual for student athletes
cards.notes: Student athletes, particularly football players, touch the bronze panther statue for good luck before heading to the field.
cards.short_summary: A pre-game superstition involving the school's bronze mascot statue.
cards.evidence_claim: Seniors established the tradition of touching the panther statue for good luck before games when football returned in 1994.
cards.source_title: ORANGE : Chapman Seniors to Unveil Mascot Statue
cards.access_notes: The statue is located outdoors near the athletics fields and is accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Winterfest Artificial Snowfall
cards.subtitle: A Southern California holiday miracle
cards.notes: Every December, the university hosts Winterfest, featuring a tree lighting and a magical artificial snowfall in the heart of campus.
cards.short_summary: An annual holiday celebration where it 'snows' in the middle of the Orange campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Winterfest includes a holiday tree lighting and artificial snowfall in the Attallah Piazza.
cards.source_title: Winterfest and Doy's Holiday Tree Lighting Kicks Off Holiday Season at Chapman
cards.access_notes: Held annually in early December; open to the community.

cards.title: The Short Story Dispenser
cards.subtitle: Instant literature at the push of a button
cards.notes: Students can get free, randomly selected 1, 3, or 5-minute stories printed on receipt-like paper from a kiosk in the library.
cards.short_summary: A unique library kiosk that provides free literary snacks to students on the go.
cards.evidence_claim: The Short Story Dispenser in Leatherby Libraries provides free, randomly selected stories to the Chapman community.
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of Leatherby Libraries; available during library hours.

cards.title: The Four Pillars Symbolism
cards.subtitle: Intellectual, Physical, Social, and Spiritual
cards.notes: The central fountain features four pillars of varying heights, representing the core values of a Chapman education.
cards.short_summary: A symbolic water feature where each pillar represents a different aspect of student development.
cards.evidence_claim: The Marion Halfacre Fountain symbolizes the 'Four Pillars' of a Chapman education: intellectual, physical, social, and spiritual.
cards.source_title: The Spiritual Pillar - Reflections by Rev. Nancy Brink
cards.access_notes: Centrally located in Attallah Piazza; illuminated with red lights at night.

cards.title: The 'Preachers' Legacy
cards.subtitle: From the pulpit to the panther
cards.notes: Before becoming the Panthers, Chapman's teams were known as the Preachers, Parsons, or Deacons due to the school's religious roots.
cards.short_summary: A nod to the university's history as a Disciples of Christ institution through its former mascot names.
cards.evidence_claim: Before adopting the panther mascot in the 1920s, Chapman teams were known as The Preachers, The Parsons, or The Deacons.
cards.access_notes: Historical tradition documented in university archives and the 'Our Story' campus history.

cards.title: The Lost Sunken Lawn
cards.subtitle: A vanished campus landmark
cards.notes: For decades, students gathered on the 'Sunken Lawn' in front of Memorial Hall before it was filled in and leveled in 2000.
cards.short_summary: A historical gathering spot that remains a point of nostalgia for older alumni.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sunken Lawn in front of Memorial Hall was filled in and leveled in 2000 to become the Bert Williams Mall.
cards.access_notes: Now the site of the Bert Williams Mall; historical context available in university archives.
